description: Community-maintained MLB National League injury database tracking updates for NL stars.

players.name: Ronald Acuña Jr.

injury_history.details: Tore right ACL two days before the 2021 All-Star break; missed remainder of 2021 season.
Tore left ACL near the end of May 2024; limited 2024 season to 49 games (.250/.324/.420, 4 HR, 15 RBI, 16 SB).
Strained left hamstring; had initially returned from a milder hamstring strain on May 19 but re-aggravated it. Hit .251 with 7 HR, 15 SB, .793 OPS in 53 games in 2025 before being placed on the IL.

rehab_timeline.details: Began Spring Training at NARF. Doing regular batting practice, throwing, and running drills in a straight line, but not yet cleared for cutting drills. Hitting long home runs in cage.
Traveled to Los Angeles for final medical clearances from doctors to build up running and begin a rehab assignment.
Expected to begin outfield work and cutting/stopping/starting in the coming days. Rehab assignment likely to begin around the All-Star break.
Expected to begin Minor League rehab assignment during the All-Star break; anticipated return shortly after.

players.return_status: Returned to Atlanta Braves leadoff spot for 2026 season; confirmed by manager Walt Weiss on Feb 22, 2026. Launched a baseball at 112.4 mph in his first spring training appearance.
players.notes: Two surgically repaired knees. Career production when healthy: .275/.394/.462 with 25 HR and 25 SB since 2023. 2023 MVP season featured a 40-70 campaign (41 HR, 73 SB).

players.name: Mookie Betts

current_injury.details: Placed on 10-day IL with right oblique strain prior to L.A.'s series-finale win over the Nationals on April 6, 2025. Felt discomfort running the bases after a checked swing during Saturday's game. MRI confirmed the oblique strain. Manager Dave Roberts initially described it as 'more moderate than significant.'

injury_history.details: Required a two-week IL stint. Betts noted his current oblique injury is less severe than that prior experience.

rehab_timeline.details: Placed on 10-day IL with right oblique strain. Hyeseong Kim recalled from Triple-A to take his spot.
Betts reported feeling 'light years ahead' of expected recovery. Dodged playing again for the next couple of days.

Suffered a minor setback in recovery — felt soreness after beginning on-field batting practice. Dodgers temporarily slowed his rehab program. Transferred to cage hitting temporarily. He reported feeling he has 'turned a corner.'
Could play in a Minor League game as soon as this weekend per manager Dave Roberts.

players.return_status: Recovering from oblique strain; rehab ahead of mid-May 2026 return. In 2026, had a slow start batting .179 through 8 games before the setback. Kim and Rojas have formed a shortstop platoon in his absence.
players.notes: Former 2018 NL MVP. Oblique injuries are notoriously finicky. Dodgers have depth at short with Kim, Rojas, and Freeland.

players.name: Freddie Freeman
players.status: Active — managing chronic ankle issues, 2026 season underway

current_injury.injury: Ankle bone bruise and sprain (postseason), requiring surgery; additional procedure planned before 2026 season
current_injury.details: Underwent ankle surgery in early December 2024 to address a bone bruise and sprain sustained during the 2024 postseason. In late 2025, reports emerged that Freeman would undergo additional procedures ahead of the 2026 season, with Andrew Friedman initially disputing the need but later reports confirming surgery is planned.

injury_history.details: Chronic ankle problems that have affected his speed. Postseason ankle injury in 2024 led to surgery. Ongoing management of the ankle condition.

rehab_timeline.details: Ankle surgery in early December 2024 for bone bruise and sprain from the 2024 postseason.

At Dodgers FanFest, Freeman stated he has yet to begin running but expressed confidence in being ready for the regular season opener (March 18, 2025 in Tokyo). Not expected to be ready for initial Cactus League games.
Played in 2025 World Series for the Dodgers, hitting a home run in Game 7 against the Blue Jays. Demonstrated his health was sufficient for postseason play.

Reports emerged that Freeman was set to undergo additional procedures ahead of the 2026 season. Team Canada manager Ernie Whitt confirmed minimal details; Andrew Friedman initially stated he didn't believe Freeman needed procedures, but subsequent reports contradicted this.
In Spring Training for 2026 season, managing ankle health under Dave Roberts' guidance to limit wear.
Struggling in 2026 with an offensive drought (only 4 HR by this date). The ankle condition may be contributing to his reduced power output.

players.return_status: Active for 2026 season but managing chronic ankle issues. Hit .282/.378/.476 in 147 games in 2023 (.331/.429/.545 in 2022). Post-2024 surgery, production has been limited by ankle health. In 2026, experiencing a notable offensive slump.
players.notes: 2024 World Series MVP. One of the premier first basemen in MLB. His ankle has been a recurring issue affecting speed and power. Dave Roberts is managing his workload to keep him healthy for a 2026 championship push.
